title: Oscar and the Thorn
premise: Emrys Winterbourne, last apprentice of the Wardens' Guild in a valley where magic is sealed away, learns that the border wards were not failing—they were murdered, sabotaged by his own guildmaster to hide the truth: the valley's peace was built on a stolen heir and an unavenged crime from the Thorn War. When the stars go out and the wards collapse, Emrys must carry the proof of that crime beyond the valley before the old enemy kingdoms use its revelation as a casus belli. Hunted by both a royal inquisitor who wants the secret buried and a rebel order that wants it weaponized, Emrys discovers he himself is the stolen heir. In the end he chooses neither crown nor rebellion, publicly surrendering the inheritance to a council of survivors and shattering the cycle—buying a fragile justice outside the law at the cost of his name, his home, and the only family he had.
about_author: Ivo Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town legal disputes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people trapped inside other people's histories.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Introduces Hollowmere valley, the dying Warden's Guild, and Emrys's quiet life tending lamps that no longer hold magic. Guildmaster Corvane assigns him the night watch on the border stones. Emotional beat: comfortable smallness, faint restlessness.

chapters.title: Lamps Without Fire
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He repairs the ward-lamps with mundane craft, hiding from Corvane that one lamp still flickers with real light. His friend Sela teases him about never leaving the valley. Beat: longing vs. duty; the first seed of the secret.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. During his watch, every star vanishes at once and the border wards fall like cut ropes. Cold air floods the valley for the first time in living memory. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What Corvane Knew
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Corvane reacts not with surprise but with practiced efficiency, burning documents in the guildhouse cellar. He orders Emrys to say nothing and gives him a sealed letter 'for if I don't return.' Beat: betrayal's first taste.

chapters.title: Sela Sees Smoke
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. From the mill she spots the guildhouse fire and riders approaching the pass—strangers wearing royal grey. She warns Emrys, forcing him to choose between obeying Corvane and fleeing. Beat: loyalty tested by evidence.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Wall
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Corvane disappears into the night. Emrys opens the letter: coordinates, a name (Veyra Thorn), and one line—'the valley was built on a grave.' Royal inquisitor Dain Marrec arrives asking questions. Beat: fear and resolve.

chapters.title: Grey Riders at the Gate
chapters.summary: Dain Marrec's POV. Marrec interrogates the villagers smoothly, charming and menacing. He suspects the guild but lacks proof. Emrys lies badly and Marrec notices. Beat: cat-and-mouse begins; reader sees the antagonist's intelligence.

chapters.title: Over the Border Stone
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys slips past the fallen wards at dawn—the first crossing in sixty years—and steps into a world humming with magic that makes him physically ill. Beat: wonder, pain, homesickness.

chapters.title: The Road of Broken Bells
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On the pilgrim road he finds villages where magic returned violently: wells that whisper, children with glowing eyes. An old hedge-witch, Maren, shelters him and reads the letter. Beat: the world is bigger and more wounded than he imagined.

chapters.title: Maren's Price
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She recognizes the Winterbourne seal and demands the truth in exchange for passage. Emrys realizes even strangers have stakes in his secret. Marrec's agents reach the village. Beat: trust as currency; narrow escape.

chapters.title: The Rebel Order
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Captured by the Ashcloaks, a rebel order descended from Thorn War survivors, led by the charismatic Veyra Thorn. They claim the letter proves royal crimes and want Emrys as their herald. Beat: seduction of a cause.

chapters.title: Veyra's Version
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. She shows Emrys ruins and mass graves from the war's end, framing the valley as a prison built to bury evidence. Her conviction is magnetic—but her methods are ruthless. Beat: doubt planted; sympathy for the enemy.

chapters.title: Marrec Closes In
chapters.summary: Dain Marrec's POV. Marrec tracks the Ashcloak camp, negotiating with a traitor within it. He reveals to the reader his own orders: recover the letter, silence everyone. Beat: rising menace; the noose tightens.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Face
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The camp is raided; the traitor is Sela, who followed him over the border and made her own bargain to protect her family. Emrys escapes with Veyra but loses the letter. Beat: heartbreak; loyalty vs. truth crystallized.

chapters.title: Chasing Paper
chapters.summary: Emrys and Veyra's alternating POV. A breakneck pursuit of Marrec's column across the moorlands. Veyra wants the letter burned or broadcast; Emrys wants to read all of it first. Beat: friction between allies; momentum.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Recovered mid-flight, the full letter reveals: the valley's founding warden stole the infant heir of House Thorn to end the war, and the Winterbourne line has guarded the lie since. Emrys does the arithmetic of bloodlines. Beat: devastating personal revelation—he is the heir.

chapters.title: Denial in the Ruins
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Shell-shocked, Emrys tests the claim against his own memories: his mother's lullabies in Old Thorn dialect, a birthmark, Corvane's tenderness. Grief for a self that may never have been real. Beat: identity crisis.

chapters.title: Veyra's Claim
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra reveals she knew—or hoped—who Emrys was when she took him in; a living heir legitimizes her rebellion. Emrys feels used twice over. Beat: the alliance fractures; manipulation exposed.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of the Silent Choir
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They shelter in a monastery of monks sworn to record history without judging it. The Abbot offers Emrys a third path: give the truth to the archive, not to armies. Beat: stillness; the theme of justice outside law takes shape.

chapters.title: Marrec's Offer
chapters.summary: Dain Marrec's POV. Marrec corners them and, surprisingly, offers Emrys amnesty: come back, be a nobody again, and the crown buries everything. He genuinely believes peace requires lies. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: Corvane Returns
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Corvane finds them, dying of wounds taken covering Emrys's escape. He confesses: he wasn't the valley's jailer but its last defender, and he chose Emrys as heir hoping he'd find a better answer than either side offered. Beat: forgiveness and grief; mentor's death.

chapters.title: Burial and Bargain
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys buries Corvane and strikes terms with Veyra: he'll stand as heir publicly once—but before a council of war survivors, not her army. Marrec, watching, sends word to his superiors. Beat: agency reclaimed; stakes raised.

chapters.title: The Road to Cindermarch
chapters.summary: Travel montage through contested lands; POV rotates among Emrys, Veyra, Marrec. Refugees, deserters, and rumors of mobilizing armies show what war would cost. Beat: urgency; the clock ticking toward catastrophe.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Crown loyalists attack; Sela reappears, saving Emrys's life and begging forgiveness. He can't give it yet, but can't refuse her help. Beat: wounded loyalty; grudging partnership.

chapters.title: The Council Refuses
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The survivor elders reject both Veyra's rebellion and Emrys's compromise, fearing truth will reignite the war regardless. Emrys realizes institutions built on the lie cannot host its reckoning. Beat: despair; plan must change.

chapters.title: Marrec's Orders Change
chapters.summary: Dain Marrec's POV. His superiors order him to assassinate Emrys rather than retrieve him—peace now means erasing the heir entirely. Marrec hesitates for the first time. Beat: antagonist's crisis of conscience.

chapters.title: The Stars Return Wrong
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Astronomers confirm the vanished stars are returning misaligned—magic itself is destabilizing because the wards were anchored to a living heir: Emrys. His existence is literally unraveling the sky. Beat: cosmic stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Sela's Confession
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. She tells Emrys the full story of her bargain and what she learned spying: the crown plans to blame the Ashcloaks for the falling sky and launch a preemptive war. Beat: truth as loyalty's final form; reconciliation begins.

chapters.title: A Plan Made of Glass
chapters.summary: Emrys, Veyra, Sela, and a reluctant Marrec convene secretly. The plan: broadcast the archive's full record—crime, theft, and all—at the winter solstice conclave, letting every faction hear it simultaneously. Beat: fragile unity; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Conclave
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Disguised as archivists, they enter Cindermarch's conclave spire. Tension, near-discoveries, Marrec vouching for them against his own colleagues. Beat: suspense; unlikely loyalties holding.

chapters.title: The Reading Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Before the assembled crowns and orders, the Silent Choir's records are read aloud: the theft, the forged peace, the buried graves. The hall fractures—outrage, denial, hunger for advantage. Beat: catharsis and chaos entwined.

chapters.title: Veyra's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Seeing chaos, Veyra seizes the moment to declare the restored Kingdom of Thorn with Emrys as figurehead, ordering her soldiers to arrest the delegations. Emrys refuses to play his part. Beat: the seduction of power rejected at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Renunciation
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On the conclave floor, Emrys publicly renounces the inheritance—not to bury it, but to dissolve it: no heir, no claim, no casus belli. The sky steadies overhead as the anchor releases. Beat: climax of theme; enormous personal cost.

chapters.title: Blades and Bells
chapters.summary: Action climax, rotating POVs. Veyra's hardliners attack; Marrec defends Emrys against his own former soldiers; Sela holds the archive door. The reading continues uninterrupted—a war fought around a voice reciting truth. Beat: peak tension.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Answer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Veyra falls—killed by her own lieutenant rather than abandon the fight. Marrec is gravely wounded shielding Emrys. The delegations, denied their pretext and confronted with shared guilt, agree to a survivor-led tribunal. Beat: victory that bleeds.

chapters.title: Tribunal of Survivors
chapters.summary: Episodic scenes, multiple POVs. The tribunal hears testimony outside any crown's law: reparations, memorials, the opening of the valley. Justice is slow, imperfect, and real. Beat: resolution of the justice theme.

chapters.title: Marrec's Choice
chapters.summary: Dain Marrec's POV. Recovering, Marrec resigns his commission and asks Emrys nothing—only to be allowed to witness the valley opened. Two enemies share a quiet drink. Beat: grace between adversaries.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys returns to Hollowmere with Sela. The wards are gone forever; magic enters gently now. Villagers confront the truth of their founders—anger, mourning, then the first honest festival in sixty years. Beat: bittersweet belonging.

chapters.title: The Lamp Still Burns
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Rebuilding the guild as a school of memory-keeping rather than secrecy, Emrys lights the lamp that first flickered with true magic. He keeps his name Winterbourne—chosen, not inherited. Beat: identity resolved on his own terms.

chapters.title: Oscar and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Coda, Emrys's POV. Years later, teaching children under returned stars, Emrys tells them the story of a boy called Oscar—a nickname his mother gave him—and the thorn that grew through a lie until someone finally pulled it. The last line mirrors the first. Beat: peace earned, story complete.
